Formulation:
Predisposing factors: Personal history of hypothyroidism; family history of suicide.  
Precipitating factors: Occupational change (new job) 2 months ago.  
Perpetuating factors: Poor sleep, decreased appetite, possible thyroid under-replacement, reduced activity.  
Protective factors: Stable marriage, intact insight, no current suicidality.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem (Low mood / possible MDD)
- Patient Goal(s): Regain previous level of energy, appetite, concentration, and enjoyment in daily life
- Clinical Goal(s): Establish definitive diagnosis (MDD vs adjustment vs medical cause); reduce depressive symptoms; restore functioning
- Actions (Patient):
  • Schedule in-person GP appointment and blood tests  
  • Monitor mood, sleep, and energy in a daily log  
  • Implement sleep hygiene strategies and maintain regular physical activity as tolerated
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Conduct full biopsychosocial assessment incl. PHQ-9 or equivalent screening  
  • Order bloods: TSH, free T4/T3, CBC, ferritin/B12, metabolic panel  
  • Discuss and consider initiating evidence-based treatment (e.g., CBT referral, SSRI if indicated)  
  • Provide psychoeducation on depression and when to seek urgent help  
  • Arrange 2–4 week follow-up to review results and symptom trajectory

Secondary Problem (Hypothyroidism – potential under-replacement)
- Patient Goal(s): Optimize physical health and energy
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm current thyroid function; adjust thyroxine dose if needed
- Actions (Patient):
  • Adhere strictly to thyroxine regimen; bring medication supply to review  
  • Report any dosing changes or missed doses
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Check recent prescription history for adherence concerns  
  • Interpret TSH/free T4 results; titrate thyroxine accordingly  
  • Educate on correct dosing (e.g., fasting administration) and importance of regular monitoring

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Rationale for blood tests, nature of depression, sleep hygiene, warning signs of worsening mood, emergency contacts
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased fatigue, further sleep disruption, emerging hopelessness, suicidal thoughts
- Coping Strategies: Structured daily routine, regular exercise, relaxation techniques, communication with spouse and GP

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Obtained verbally
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: To be provided at in-person visit
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently; consider psychology referral
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 4 weeks or sooner if symptoms escalate

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Major Depressive Disorder / Adjustment Disorder – High likelihood: Symptoms meet multiple DSM-5 criteria; onset with job stressor
- Sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism – Medium likelihood: Known condition with overlapping somatic and mood symptoms
- Anemia (iron/B12 deficiency) – Medium-Low likelihood: Fatigue and exertional dyspnea; dietary intake decreased

Quality checks
● Missing elements: BMI, substance use details, formal mood scale scores, vital signs—plan includes obtaining these at in-person visit  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx  
● Transcript quality: Audio clear; minor freezes noted but content adequate for plan formulation
